finding: Lactation stage, gestational age and delivery mode all influence the composition of several bacteria inhabiting breast milk, including Bifidobacterium, Lactobacillus, Staphylococcus, Streptococcus and Enterococcus spp., and consequently, may affect the infant's early intestinal colonization.
mod_finding: Higher bacterial concentrations in colostrum and transitional milk were found in Cesarean sections, but Bifidobacterium was detected more frequently in vaginal than in Cesarean deliveries.
